commits.message: Add note about website to README

Actually fix flaky Figwheel behavior

Previous changes to downgrade figwheel-sidecar and to add
:http-server-root did not fix the problem and turned out to be
completely unrelated. It turns out that Figwheel, when launched via
Figwheel Sidecar (but not when launched via lein-figwheel), does not
serve files from resources/ unless the directory exists *before*
starting Figwheel.

Checking resources/ into version control and removing it from
:clean-targets should fix this flaky behavior. An ideal solution would
be to make Figwheel work even if resources/ does not exist when it is
launched, but in the meantime this fix will ensure correct behavior.

Since the previous fixes were misguided and introduced unneeded
complexity, they are reverted in this commmit.

Fix Emacs integration with Figwheel

Previously, an odd behavior was being observed where if Figwheel was
started from within a REPL or within Emacs, it could exist to an
existing page but when the page was reloaded, it would get a 404 error
for main.js.

Adding the :http-server-root key to the :figwheel config in project.clj
fixes this issue.

Add ClojureScript, Reagent, Figwheel

Use ClojureScript and Reagent to render the splash page, and call
through to said ClojureScript code from puzzles.web.server. Use Hiccup
to render the base HTML in puzzles.web.server.

The server can now be started in any of the following ways:
* lein do clean, figwheel
* lein do clean, cljsbuild once, repl --> (puzzles.web.server/start)
* lein do clean, cljsbuild once, run -m puzzles.web.server
* lein do clean, uberjar && heroku local

Figwheel will host a server on port 3449, while any of the other options
will use port 5000. Figwheel is the best option for development, while
using Heroku is the best way to verify that deployment will go smoothly.

Use :main for uberjar

This simplifies the Procfile considerably.
Disable Travis CI email for successful builds

Remove the :main declaration from project.clj

It doesn't make sense for libraries to have a :main namespace set, and removing
this declaration eliminates the potentially confusing warning message "Warning:
The Main-Class specified does not exist within the jar. It may not be
executable as expected. A gen-class directive may be missing in the namespace
which contains the main method" generated by 'lein uberjar' when deploying to
Heroku.

Add Heroku support

* Add Procfile
* Enable AOT compilation for improved speed when deployed
* Specify a fixed name for the uberjar to allow the Procfile command to
  find it. If this isn't done then 'heroku local' fails with "Error:
  Could not find or load main class clojure.main".
* Require Leiningen 2 to allow uberjar compilation to work properly when
  deployed. If this isn't done then the app fails with the same error as
  above when deployed.
* Allow configuring the port number using the $PORT environment variable
  so that the server can connect to the port expected by Heroku. If this
  isn't done, then the app fails when deployed with the error "Error R10
  (Boot timeout) -> Web process failed to bind to $PORT within 60
  seconds of launch".

Add Procfile and enable AOT compilation.

Simplify puzzles.web functions

Replace 'start-new-server' and 'restart-server' with 'stop' and 'start'
in puzzles.web, and prevent the server from being started as soon as the
namespace is loaded. This interface is simpler and more flexible. Also,
allow starting the server using 'lein run -m puzzles.web'.
Add Travis CI build status icon to README

Add .travis.yml

Set up Travis CI to run tests automatically on pushing to Github.
Correct reference to sample KenKen puzzles

Add README.md

Add a summary and some example usage.

Add puzzles.core

Add a :main namespace so that all the namespaces can be accessed easily
as soon as a REPL is started.

Add note to README

Note that C-c C-k is unnecessary when running Figwheel Sidecar in Emacs,
as Clojure code is automatically reloaded on save by Figwheel.

Fix flaky Figwheel behavior

It turns out that Figwheel, when launched via Figwheel Sidecar (but not
when launched via lein-figwheel), does not serve files from resources/
unless the directory exists *before* starting Figwheel.

Checking resources/ into version control and removing it from
:clean-targets should fix this flaky behavior. An ideal solution would
be to make Figwheel work even if resources/ does not exist when it is
launched, but in the meantime this fix will ensure correct behavior.

Since previous attempts to fix the problem (by adding :http-server-root
and downgrading figwheel-sidecar) were misguided and introduced unneeded
complexity, they are reverted in this commit.

Also, the README was updated to reflect the dependency upgrades.
Use different keywords for blocks of same shape

Fix critical bug in all_bitstrings

A major oversight in this function caused it to be unable to return any
bitstrings starting with a zero! This commit fixes that.

Move all_bitstrings and result_words to top

It makes no sense for these to be *below* the definition of takingInput.
They should have been moved up at the same time as the latter function.

Fix bug in tm_stateTrans2

It looked like the final 'return False' was unneeded, so I had removed
it in one of my previous cleanups. Unfortunately, the control flow is so
weird in this code that I missed a path, allowing tm_stateTrans2 to
return None in some cases where it was supposed to return False. This
should fix that bug.

Use takingInput in place of tm_takingInput

This addresses about 1% of the code duplication in this file, but it's a
step in the right direction.
Move definition of takingInput to top of file
Allow 'accept' and 'reject' to be in past tense

Improve output formatting

Instead of printing weird Python data structures, print a properly
human-readable message when a test fails. Also, exit immediately on test
failure, since this code is targeted at ensuring that an NFA is
functioning correctly, rather than grading an NFA.

Get command-line usage working end-to-end

This involved fixing a few bugs that were introduced in the various
refactorings, as well as adding a hook to allow the script to be run
from the command line.

Expand allowable syntax in test files

In particular, the original syntax (where only 'reject' was processed
and 'accept' was ignored, and the parsing was primarily driven by how
many spaces there were in the line(!)) has been thrown out completely in
favor of something more sane, where the following types of test cases
are allowable:

1010 -> accept
01 rej
empty->yes

Also, you can embed Python code directly into the test files, provided
that it takes the form of a function declaration for 'check' or 'words'.
The former function, if declared, will be used to compute the desired
result (True for accept and False for reject) for any test cases where
you don't specify the desired result, i.e.

empty
101

The latter function, if declared, should return a list of additional
inputs whose desired results are computed using 'check'. In addition to
the Python standard library, it has access to the 'all_bitstrings'
function, which returns a list of all possible bitstrings of length no
greater than its argument (in lexicographic order).

The exact format of test files will be documented in README.md in the
future.

Clean up jflapgrader.py

The original version of this file was, quite frankly, atrocious. It had
tons of commented-out debugging statements; inconsistent indentation;
egregious spacing; some of the silliest comments I've ever seen in my
life; imports in the middle of the file (and nested inside functions!);
absolutely no consistent style conventions; a large commented-out
subscript at the bottom; and quite a few more problems to boot.

I've done my best to remove all these problems. The complete lack of
useful documentation, the obscenely chosen variable names, the
everything-as-globals programming style, and the fact that several
hundred lines are copy/pasted but changed subtly still make the code
rather formidable, but I tried to stick to non-semantic changes in this
commit.

Import jflapgrader.py and license from HMC-Grader

The original version of jflapgrader.py can be found at [1]. Note that
line endings were changed to CRLF using 'git config core.autocrlf'.

[1]: https://github.com/CSGreater-Developers/HMC-Grader/blob/f7ce1fe866fcde521c0a2dcb5102a75fae223142/app/plugins/autograder/jflapgrader.py

Add MIT license
